text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A tender for concessions of land in the free trade zone of Braila will be held on November 27.
ADEVARUL
- U.S. oil company Amoco gave up oil product marketing in Romania, Bulgaria and Poland as part of plans to develop its business in North, South and Central America.
- CEC savings bank, creditor of troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA, demands that the bank pay back its outstanding debts to CEC with priority.
- German company Henkel has started to produce Rex detergents at a plant in the Danube port town of Galati.
- The government decided to allot 34.7 billion lei from the state budget for investment and unfinished repair works.
TINERETUL LIBER

- Parliament's lower house, the Chamber of Deputies, approved a draft law allowing the central bank to give credits to troubled banks Dacia Felix and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA to help them redeem small depositors.
ZIUA
- The Bucharest public transport authority RATB 's unpaid bills to suppliers amount to 11 billion lei.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The Chamber of Deputies approved the introduction of the GSM telephone system in Romania. The licence tax is $50 million for 10 years.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes the list of candidates of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc for the November 3 parliamentary elections.
- The Students' League said the Constitutional Court's decision to allow President Ion Iliescu to run for office in the November elections shows the justice system serves ruling interests.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The poor-quality campaign videos presented by the 16 presidential candidates on state television, underscore lack of professionalism of the candidates and their electoral staff, Ion Cristoiu says in an editorial.
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on the arms trafficking scandal recently disclosed in Italy, allegedly involving a Romanian minister.
- A printing house in the eastern town of Braila printed notebooks for schoolchildren with three roses on the cover, the electoral sign of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
- Prosecutors in Romania have big problems, as the crime rate has tripled over the past six years, says general prosecutor Nicolae Cochinescu in a one-page interview.
ADEVARUL
- Hundreds of Romanians hoping to work abroad queue at the Caritas hospital in Bucharest, the country's sole institution authorised to issue special medical certificates.
- The 1.6 million eligible Bucharest voters will cast ballots at 1,338 polling stations.
- The police confiscated 4,700 kg of various drugs this year, says the newspaper in a one-page report on the rising drug trafficking and abuse problem in Romania.
- The police have filed 6,181 corruption cases to the prosecution this year alone, says Romania's police chief Costica Voicu.
ZIUA
- The newspaper publishes a letter by the International Committee for Protection of Journalists asking President Iliescu to stop harassing Romanian journalists.

- In a four-page supplement addressed to the country's rural residents, critical to deciding the outcome of the November 3 elections, the newspaper urges them to vote for one of the three main opposition presidential candidates.
AZI

- Romania has no law on ministerial responsability, so members of Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu's government are looking to enter parliament, says the newspaper in a comment on how all ministers are running for seats in the November 3 parliamentary elections.
LIBERTATEA
- The police dismanteled a gang of drug traffickers by arresting a Turk, a Syrian and two Romanian women.
COTIDIANUL

- The National Broadcasting Committee (CNA) barred the private television Antena 1 from broadcasting interviews with voters, alleging it would infringe the secrecy of the vote. ($=3,262 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
